episodes.169464: A shortwave led to the development of scattered thunderstorms in a strongly unstable environment late afternoon into evening. Several of these storms produced severe damaging wind gusts.
episodes.169574: Shortwave moved through the southwesterly flow aloft that's been parked over the area this week and set off another round of severe thunderstorms over the area this afternoon into the overnight hours.
episodes.169592: With an area of high pressure centered to the east of New Mexico, the monsoonal moisture plume was oriented southwest to northeast across the state on July 7, 2022. Meanwhile, drier air filtering in from the west effectively shut down convection in this area. This focused the daily round of thunderstorms across the south central mountains with the McBride burn scar being most at risk for flash flooding and debris flow impacts. As thunderstorms developed in that area, flash flooding along with debris was reported along Eagle Creek Road near Alto.
episodes.169602: Thunderstorms developed along the higher terrain to the north and moved towards the area. As storms moved into a highly unstable environment, they became more widespread and produced damaging winds, small hail, and flash flooding.
episodes.169603: Thunderstorms developed along the higher terrain to the north and moved towards the area. As storms moved into a highly unstable environment, they became more widespread and produced damaging winds, small hail, and flash flooding.
episodes.169757: Heavy rainfall from thunderstorms led to isolated instances of flooding.
episodes.169917: A stationary boundary was elongated from west to east across the state on the 7th. While the more widespread showers and thunderstorms were located in southern Indiana crossing into north-central Kentucky during the early evening, there were some additional stronger showers and thunderstorms loacted across the southeast of the state as well. One of these storms went through McCreary County, resulting in multiple trees being downed in and around the Strunk community.
episodes.170053: Disturbances moved through a persistent southwest flow aloft across the region, which continued to provide daily afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms. These storms, some of which were severe, brought strong, gusty winds, severe hail, heavy localized rainfall, and lightning.
episodes.170413: A few strong thunderstorms developed over the Nebraska Panhandle during the afternoon of the 7th. This included a line of severe thunderstorms moving southeast out of southwest South Dakota with strong winds and hail impacting portions of Dawes County.
episodes.170514: Areas south of a stationary front within the lower Ohio Valley warmed into the mid 80's to the mid 90's. The air mass was very moist, with dew points in the lower to mid 70's. Instability was quite strong, with mixed-layer capes around 3000. Minimal wind shear inhibited thunderstorm organization. A storm pulsed up to severe levels, producing isolated damaging winds. Weak steering winds resulted in slow storm movement and an isolated flash flood.
episodes.170515: Areas south of a stationary front over the Missouri Valley warmed into the mid 80's to the mid 90's. The air mass was very moist, with dew points in the lower to mid 70's. Instability was quite strong, with mixed-layer capes around 3000. Minimal wind shear inhibited thunderstorm organization. A storm pulsed up to severe levels, producing isolated damaging winds.
episodes.170552: A flash flood was observed along Cedar Creek to the confluence of the Big Thompson River and Highway 34. Debris accumulated behind a bridge along an access road to a neighborhood on Cedar Brook Lane. A significant debris flow continued down Cedar Creek to Cedar Lane.  Fifteen residents were stranded temporarily. Minor flooding was observed along a private road near Masonville.
episodes.170585: A surface low for a few days July 7th and 8th. While the parameter space was not conducive to strong convection, the steep lapse rates, low LCLs, and sufficient 0-3 km CAPE resulted in a favorable environment for funnel cloud development both days. Several funnel clouds were reported across central and northern Iowa, along with two tornadoes documented under developing storms during the afternoon of July 7th.  These spin-ups remained in open areas with little damage. Storms were also efficient rain producers, with a pocket of 3 to 5 inches in Hardin and Grundy counties.
episodes.170608: An isolated but intense thunderstorm resulted in widespread wind damage in and near the City of Staunton during the afternoon hours. Later that evening, a brief supercell produced localized wind damage in Prince William County.
episodes.170656: Severe thunderstorms produced six short-lived tornadoes across northeast Weld and Morgan counties.  Two of those landspouts were rated as EF1.  In Weld County, the tornado downed several trees and power poles.  In Morgan County, some oak trees were shredded and a power pole was snapped.  Across Douglas, Elbert and northern Lincoln counties, severe thunderstorms produced large hail, from quarter to half dollar size.  Strong thunderstorm wind gusts to 60 mph were reported along highway 71, south of Limon.
episodes.170916: A couple of severe thunderstorms produced some quarter size hail and flash flooding.
episodes.171101: Isolated storms developed across Delmarva early in the morning. One storm resulted in a downed tree in Queen Anne's County, MD.
episodes.171262: A thunderstorm became severe over the southern Black Hills and tracked southeast across parts of southwestern South Dakota. The storm produced wind gusts over 60 mph.
episodes.171330: An isolated severe thunderstorm caused some wind damage.
episodes.171507: Multiple rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms moved across Kentucky between July 6th and July 8th. The main focus for convection was areas along and just south of a quasi-stationary surface front, initially positioned from west to east across central Indiana on July 6th. Each afternoon, thunderstorms developed in the unstable airmass, gradually pushing south and east before dissipating quickly after loss of daytime heating. On July 6th, a broken line of strong-to-severe thunderstorms crossed the Ohio River from Indiana during the mid-afternoon hours. As the storms pushed across central Kentucky, downdraft CAPE of greater than 1200 J/kg helped damaging wind gusts reach the ground, and several wind damage reports were observed, mainly across north central Kentucky. On July 7th, lesser instability led to the development of garden-variety thunderstorms, with wind damage only being observed in a few of the strongest cells. Finally, on July 8th, clusters of strong and severe thunderstorms produced scattered wind damage across south central Kentucky, with flash flooding also being observed in Russell County due to repeated bursts of heavy rainfall.
episodes.171509: Thunderstorms produced torrential rainfall that led to flash flooding from the evening of July 6 into the morning of July 7 in parts of the panhandle as well as central Nebraska.
episodes.171581: A complex of thunderstorms developed along a stalled frontal boundary over Missouri during the pre-dawn hours of July 7, 2022. These storms progressed into Illinois, producing isolated flooding in eastern Illinois during the early afternoon.
episodes.171614: A slow moving thunderstorm complex produced very heavy rain and localized flash flooding across portions of Morrill and Box Butte counties late in the evening on the 6th into the early morning hours on the 7th.
episodes.171667: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed across southeast South Carolina along a surface trough in the early evening hours. One thunderstorms produced isolated wind damage in Colleton County.
episodes.171668: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed in the early afternoon hours along the sea breeze on the southeast Georgia coast. One thunderstorm became severe, producing wind damage in Chatham County.
episodes.171980: An open wave moving up from the south initiated multiple hail producing storms, and at least one with estimated severe winds.
episodes.172095: During the afternoon hours on the 6th, isolated storms developed over Eastern Colorado and evolved into a line of storms that moved east into Northwest Kansas through the night. These storms produced wind gusts estimated up to 60 mph across Cheyenne County, Colorado along with up to penny sized hail and heavy rain up to 4.5 inches. The heaviest rainfall amounts were reported in the eastern half of Cheyenne County with reports of visibility as low as one-eight of a mile at times. The heavy rain also caused some road flooding on a county road southwest of Arapahoe, Colorado that lasted through the late morning hours on the 8th. No damage was reported from these storms.
episodes.172105: An active tropical wave moved across the area. This wave brought periods of heavy rainfall, along with strong gusty winds, resulting in multiple flood reports.
episodes.172200: Thunderstorms developed in the afternoon over and near the higher terrain, with an initial risk of strong to severe storms in the Pikes Peak region. This risk then spread into the eastern plains along the Highway 50 corridor later in the evening, where large hail damaging wind gusts up to around 75 mph, localized flash flooding, and even a tornado occurred.
episodes.172239: An isolated supercell produced large hail up to two and half inches in diameter, and wind gusts to 80 mph across portions of Barton and Rice counties in central Kansas on July 6th, 2022.
episodes.172281: Thunderstorms produced isolated severe weather and heavy rainfall. A wind gust of 62 mph was observed one mile east-southeast of Bowdle, and quarter-size hail was reported one mile west of Zell. A measured rainfall amount of 5.5 inches by the public occurred one mile southeast of Loyalton. Estimated 3.50 inches of rain was reported at Bowdle, as well as 3 inches at Selby, Roscoe, and Miranda. Funnel clouds were reported near Highmore and Carpenter.
episodes.172354: A surface to mid level ridge axis extended across the I-10 corridor Thursday afternoon. There was an early start to convection across SE GA where lingering outflow boundaries spawned initial inland storms over a moist and unstable airmass under west-northwest steering flow. The east coast sea breeze was pinned along the I-95 corridor as the dominant west coast sea breeze shifted inland in the afternoon. Storms zippered southward from Camden/Glynn counties into NE FL as the sea breeze and outflow boundaries converged. Isolated strong storms developed along these boundary collisions producing gusts of 40 to 45 mph along the I-95 corridor. With a saturated airmass and slow storm motion, locally heavy rain of 3 to 4 inches fell in Glynn, Camden and Nassau counties.
episodes.172355: A surface to mid level ridge axis extended across the I-10 corridor Thursday afternoon. episodes.172480: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a frontal boundary produced damaging winds across portions of central and south central Virginia.
episodes.172551: During the afternoon and evening, a few clusters of thunderstorms moved southeast across East Tennessee. Some isolated wind damage occurred with these clusters.
episodes.172596: Strong diurnal heating along with dewpoints in the upper 60s to mid 70s contributed to a highly unstable airmass. Multiple clusters of thunderstorms formed in the afternoon, resulting in damaging winds across southwest Virginia.
episodes.172604: A stalled frontal boundary to the north from the Mid-Mississippi Valley into the Ohio Valley and northern Virginia led to early morning storms north of the Carolinas. This led to numerous surface boundaries that aided thunderstorms to form along the Piedmont in the mid to late-afternoon hours. These storms tracked east-southeast in the evening to early overnight hours into the Sandhills and Coastal Plain. Many of the storms produced thunderstorm wind damage and a few also produced flash flooding.
episodes.172618: Near the end of the first week of the month, isolated Flash Flooding occurred in central Utah.
episodes.172634: Morning thunderstorms over the Ohio Valley, as well as a surface trough over the western Piedmont, led to several boundaries where afternoon and evening thunderstorms formed across central North Carolina. The storms formed over the western Piedmont and over Virginia, tracking into the central and eastern Piedmont and Coastal Plain in the mid to late-evening hours. The storms reached the far eastern portions of North Carolina in the early overnight hours. Numerous trees and wind damage was reported as a result of these thunderstorms.
episodes.172670: A narrow and nearly stationary band of thunderstorms developed across Dixon and northern Dakota Counties during the late afternoon hours. Rainfall estimates of 3 to 5 inches occurred in a very small area from central Dixon to far northwestern Woodbury Counties, with the largest observed rainfall of 5.50 inches 4 miles west of McCook Lake, 2.77 inches at mesonet site AV951 in northern Sioux City, IA, 2.07 inches at river gage SXCI4 along Perry Creek in northern Sioux City, IA 2.01 inches in Concord, NE and 1.80 inches 3 miles southwest of Jefferson, SD.

episodes.172860: Heavy rain moved through northern Missouri during the early morning hours on July 7. While there were no notable impacts across the area, there was some isolated flash flooding, which resulted in a water rescue in St. Joseph.

episodes.172919: Multiple storm clusters developed near the Blue Ridge escarpment during the afternoon and moved southeast across upstate South Carolina. A few of the embedded storms produced locally damaging wind gusts.
episodes.172983: Numerous intense severe thunderstorms developed across northern Middle Tennessee during the late morning hours of July 7 and spread southeastward into the afternoon. Many reports of large hail and wind damage were received.
episodes.173023: An area of thunderstorms moved across Eastern North Carolina on the evening of July 6th and produced wind damage across part of the area.
episodes.173066: Multiple disturbances moving out of the Ohio River Valley into the area set off multiple lines of strong to severe storms within an unstable and moist airmass during the late evening of July 6th and afternoon of July 7th. These storms produced scattered reports of trees and powerlines down across portions of north and central Georgia.
